properties.title: Flood Advisory issued July 23 at 7:28PM EDT until July 23 at 9:45PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Nuisance stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
ongoing.

* WHERE...North Central Union NC County in the piedmont of North
Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 945 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to streams
and other poor-drainage areas, including farmland, parks,
greenways, boat-access areas, golf courses, underpasses, and
parking lots.  Isolated, shallow flows over roadways is possible.
A few flood-prone, low-water crossings may become impassible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 710 PM EDT, Elevated streamflows continue following the heavy
rainfall that occurred earlier this morning across the Crooked
Creek watershed.  An NC Emergency Management streamgauge on the
North Fork Crooked Creek at Idlewild Rd in Hemby Bridge indicates
North Fork Crooked Creek has crested, but remains well out of its
banks up- and downstream of Hemby Bridge.  As a result, NF
Crooked Creek continues to flood adjacent low-lying farmland and
wooded areas.  While inundation may be up to 1-2 feet deep in
these locations, no impacts to structures or roadways are
expected.  However, because flooding continues, a Flood Advisory
will remain in effect through 9pm to allow North Fork Crooked
Creek to recede below bankfull.

- An axis of light to moderate rainfall is currently impacting
areas just west of the Advisory across eastern Mecklenburg
County.  Showers responsible for this rainfall will approach the
Crooked Creek watershed over the next hour, but are not expected
to strengthen.  Therefore, while isolated areas of poor-drainage
ponding may develop, this rainfall is not expected to exacerbate
ongoing high streamflows.

The threat for more significant flooding will continue to
decrease through the rest of the evening and overnight period.

- Some locations that may experience nuisance floodinginclude...
Hemby Bridge.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Asherton.

* WHEN...Until early Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 29.0 feet, Widespread major flooding threatens
livestock over a large area of the flood plain. A mile of Farm to
Market 190 near the river is flooded and flow is within a foot of
the Farm to Market 190 bridge floor over the Nueces River. The
Nueces River and Turkey Creek are a mile and a half wide south and
west of Carrizo Springs.

- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours

early Sunday morning and continue falling to 10.4 feet early
Tuesday afternoon.

28.6 feet on 07/17/1990.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.
